prompt: A regex that matches US phone numbers in any of these forms: '(123) 456-7890', '123-456-7890', '123.456.7890'. Reject any other formatting and partial matches. Output ONLY the regex (no slashes, no quotes).

A regex that matches a strong password: at least 8 characters, contains at least one lowercase letter, one uppercase letter, one digit, and one of !@#$%^&*. Reject anything missing one of those. Output ONLY the regex.
A regex that matches an ISO date 'YYYY-MM-DD' for years 1900..2099, months 01..12, days 01..31. No need to validate days-per-month. Output ONLY the regex.
A regex that matches a CSS hex color: '#' followed by exactly 3 or 6 hex digits. Case insensitive. Output ONLY the regex.

A regex that matches a semver version: MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH where each is one or more digits, optionally followed by a hyphen and a pre-release tag of letters/digits/dots (e.g., 'beta.1'). Output ONLY the regex.
A regex that matches an IPv4 address: four octets 0..255 separated by dots. Reject octets outside the range. Output ONLY the regex.
A regex that matches an email ending in '.edu' (e.g., 'name@dept.uni.edu'). Local part: letters, digits, dots, underscores, hyphens. Domain: letters, digits, hyphens, dots. Output ONLY the regex.
A regex that matches a MAC address: six pairs of hex digits separated by colons or hyphens (consistent separator). Output ONLY the regex.

A regex that matches a UK postcode in canonical form 'LETTER+DIGIT+ DIGIT+LETTER+LETTER' loosely: 1-2 letters, 1-2 digits (with optional letter at end of first part), space, then digit and 2 letters. e.g., 'SW1A 1AA', 'M1 1AE', 'EC1A 1BB'. Case insensitive. Output ONLY the regex.

A regex that matches a string of letters wrapped in matching single parentheses, optionally with a single inner pair, e.g., '(abc)' or '(ab(c)d)'. Reject mismatched or deeper nesting. Output ONLY the regex.
A regex that matches a non-negative integer with no leading zeros (single zero is fine). Output ONLY the regex.
A regex that matches a lowerCamelCase identifier: starts with a lowercase letter, then any letters/digits, must contain at least one uppercase letter (so not pure lowercase). Output ONLY the regex.
A regex that matches a 24-hour time HH:MM where HH is 00..23 and MM is 00..59. Output ONLY the regex.
A regex that matches a git short SHA: exactly 7 hex characters, lowercase only. Output ONLY the regex.
A regex that matches a non-empty line with no tab characters. Anchor it. Output ONLY the regex.
A regex that matches a URL slug: lowercase letters, digits, and hyphens, no leading or trailing hyphen, no consecutive hyphens. Output ONLY the regex.
A regex that matches a single HTML attribute of the form key="value" OR key='value' where key is letters/digits/hyphens and the quote characters must match. Output ONLY the regex.
A regex that matches a signed scientific-notation float with optional sign, mandatory decimal point, and mandatory exponent. e.g., '1.5e10', '-3.14E-2', '+0.0e0'. Output ONLY the regex.

A regex that matches a single CSV field: either an unquoted run of characters with no commas/quotes/newlines, or a double-quoted string in which a literal double-quote is escaped as "". Output ONLY the regex.
A regex matching the prefix YYYY-MM of an ISO date for years 2000..2099 and months 01..12. Output ONLY the regex.
A regex that matches an absolute http or https URL with no query or fragment, e.g. 'https://example.com/path'. Reject ftp, missing scheme, or paths only. Output ONLY the regex.
A regex for a fully-expanded IPv6 address: eight groups of exactly four hex digits separated by colons. No ::-shorthand. Output ONLY the regex.
A regex that matches a non-negative even integer with no leading zeros (0 itself is fine). Output ONLY the regex.
A regex that matches a 4-letter palindrome over lowercase letters (positions 1=4 and 2=3), e.g. 'abba', 'noon'. Output ONLY the regex.
A regex for a UTC ISO datetime exactly in the form YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ for years 2000..2099, months 01..12, days 01..31, hours 00..23, minutes/seconds 00..59. Output ONLY the regex.
A regex for a snake_case identifier: lowercase letters, digits, underscores, must start with a letter, no double underscores, no trailing underscore. Output ONLY the regex.
A regex that matches a single English word made of lowercase letters that contains at least three consecutive vowels (aeiou). Output ONLY the regex.
A regex matching a year of the form '1234 BCE' or '1234 CE' where the number is 1 to 4 digits with no leading zeros (zero year not allowed). Output ONLY the regex.
A regex matching exactly 'yes', 'no', or 'maybe' (case-insensitive), and nothing else. Output ONLY the regex.
A regex for kebab-case: lowercase letters and digits separated by single hyphens, no leading/trailing hyphen, no double hyphens, must contain at least one hyphen. Output ONLY the regex.
A regex matching a string consisting of doubled letters: a 6-character lowercase string where each pair of adjacent characters is the same letter (e.g. 'aabbcc'). Output ONLY the regex.
A regex matching a US dollar amount like $1,234.56 or $0.99: leading $, optional thousands grouped with commas, mandatory two-decimal cents. Output ONLY the regex.

A regex matching a single non-nested HTML element with matching open/close tag for one of {b, i, em, strong}, no attributes, with arbitrary text inside that doesn't contain '<' or '>'. Output ONLY the regex.
A regex matching a 2-to-5 character all-uppercase acronym (no digits, no punctuation). Output ONLY the regex.
A regex matching an image filename ending in .png, .jpg, or .jpeg (case-insensitive). The base name is at least one letter/digit/_/-. Output ONLY the regex.
A regex matching a US social security number in the form NNN-NN-NNNN. Output ONLY the regex.
A regex matching a non-empty string of lowercase letters with no three identical consecutive letters (e.g. 'aab' is fine, 'aaab' is not). Output ONLY the regex.
A regex matching a single C++ line comment: '//' followed by any characters except newline, with no leading whitespace. Output ONLY the regex.
A regex for a JSON number: optional minus, no leading zeros (or just 0), optional decimal part, optional exponent (e/E with optional sign). Output ONLY the regex.
